prompt: Completa: '____ esci stasera?' [with whom]

must_not_include.note: Italian fronts the preposition (Con chi?); it never leaves it stranded at the end as English does ('...who with?').

explanation: Who are you going out with tonight? = Con chi esci stasera? English can push the little linking word (with) to the end of a question, but Italian keeps the preposition together with its question word at the front: Con chi...? The pair moves as one, so an Italian question never ends on the preposition.

prompt: Completa: '____ hai dato le chiavi?' [to whom]

must_not_include.note: The preposition a comes first: A chi...?, not 'Chi...a?'.

explanation: Who did you give the keys to? = A chi hai dato le chiavi? The keys go to a person, and Italian marks that person with the preposition a (to) placed in front of chi: A chi...? The question word chi stays the same; the preposition in front is what makes it 'to whom'.

prompt: Completa: '____ è questa borsa?' [whose]

must_not_include.note: 'Whose' is di chi, not bare chi: the preposition di carries the possessive sense.

explanation: Whose bag is this? = Di chi è questa borsa? Italian has no single word for 'whose'; it builds the idea from di (of) plus chi (who): Di chi è...?, literally 'of whom is...?'. Drop the di and you are left with plain 'who', a different question, so the di is doing the possessive work.
examiner_note: The bare-chi guard is nested inside the correct 'di chi', but the positive is checked first and wins, so it only fires on the forgot-di attempt (ordering-protected, criterion 18 exempt case).

prompt: Completa: '____ è questo regalo?' [who ... for]

must_not_include.note: The preposition per comes first: Per chi...?, never '...chi per?'.

explanation: Who is this present for? = Per chi è questo regalo? The gift is meant for a person, and Italian puts that relationship first with per (for) before chi: Per chi...? Once again chi does not change; the preposition per carries the 'for whom' meaning.

prompt: Quale forma completa la frase? '____ leggi in estate?'

markpoints.label: only che directly before a noun

explanation: What books do you read in summer? = Che libri leggi in estate? Only che can sit directly in front of a noun. Cosa and che cosa ask 'what' on their own, but they cannot lean on a following noun the way che can, so it is Che libri..., never 'Cosa libri...'. When a noun comes straight after, reach for che.
examiner_note: Full-phrase MCQ options so the positive 'che libri' does not substring-match the 'che cosa libri' distractor. Left visible: the options already expose the candidate set.

prompt: Completa: '____ comincia il film?' [at what time]

must_not_include.note: Asking WHEN needs a che ora; bare 'Che ora?' asks what the time IS, a different question.

explanation: What time does the film start? = A che ora comincia il film? Italian asks about clock time with the set phrase a che ora (literally 'at what hour'). The a is part of the phrase and cannot be dropped: A che ora...?, not 'Che ora comincia...?', which would ask what the time is rather than when something happens.
examiner_note: The 'che ora' guard is nested in the correct 'a che ora' but the positive wins first, so it only fires on the dropped-a attempt.

prompt: Completa: '____ una password sicura?' [what is]

any_phrases.note: Understood, but Italian normally elides before è: cos'è.

explanation: What is a secure password? = Cos'è una password sicura? When cosa meets the verb è (is), the two run together and cosa loses its final -a: cosa è becomes cos'è. You will also hear the fuller che cos'è, with che added in front. The elided cos'è is the everyday form; the full cosa è sounds stiff.
examiner_note: norm() folds the apostrophe to a space, so cos'è and cos è mark identically; the elision is taught here, not graded. Accent on è is soft (fold-rescue + orthography miss).

prompt: Completa: '____ sono i tuoi colori preferiti?' (quale)

must_not_include.note: With a plural (colori), quale becomes quali: it agrees in number.

explanation: Which are your favourite colours? = Quali sono i tuoi colori preferiti? Quale changes for number: one thing keeps quale, two or more take quali. The colours here are plural (colori), so the question opens with quali. Quale agrees only in number, not gender, so quali serves masculine and feminine alike.

prompt: Completa: '____ la capitale d'Italia?' (quale)

must_not_include.note: Before è, quale drops its -e to qual: qual è, never 'quale è'.

explanation: What is the capital of Italy? = Qual è la capitale d'Italia? Before the verb è, quale drops its final -e and becomes qual. This is a bare drop, not an elision, so it takes NO apostrophe: the correct spelling is qual è, never 'qual'è'. The -e is simply gone, with nothing to mark the gap.
examiner_note: The apostrophe fold means qual'è and qual è are indistinguishable to the marker; the no-apostrophe rule is taught in the explanation, gradable only in translation. 'quale è' (unelided) is a real miss and is guarded.

prompt: Completa: '____ colore preferisci?' (quale)

markpoints.label: quale stays singular before a singular noun

must_not_include.note: With a singular noun (colore), quale stays singular: quale colore, not 'quali colore'.

explanation: Which colour do you prefer? = Quale colore preferisci? With a single thing, quale keeps its full singular form: one colour (colore, singular) takes quale. Compare the plural, where it shifts to quali colori. The ending tracks number, and nothing else.
examiner_note: Same-surface pair with interr_quale_01 (plural quali): opposite answers on the same agreement axis.

prompt: Completa: 'Vorrei un gelato. ____ mi consigli?' (quale)

markpoints.label: quale as a standalone pronoun (which one)

must_not_include.note: A single ice cream is being chosen, so the singular quale is right, not quali.

explanation: I'd like an ice cream. Which one do you recommend? = Vorrei un gelato. Quale mi consigli? Quale can stand on its own, with no noun after it, to mean 'which one' when you choose from a known set (here, the ice creams on offer). It still points at a single item, so it stays singular: quale, not quali.

prompt: Completa: '____ anni hai?' (quanto)

must_not_include.note: Quanto agrees with what it counts; anni is masculine plural, so quanti.

explanation: How old are you? = Quanti anni hai? Italian asks age by counting years, and quanto agrees with the noun it counts. Anni is masculine plural, so quanto becomes quanti, literally 'how many years do you have?'.

prompt: Completa: '____ persone vengono alla cena?' (quanto)

must_not_include.note: Persone is feminine plural, so quanto takes quante, not the masculine quanti.

explanation: How many people are coming to dinner? = Quante persone vengono alla cena? Quanto agrees with the noun it measures. Persone is feminine plural, so it takes quante. The word persona is feminine even when it refers to men.

prompt: Completa: '____ acqua bevi al giorno?' (quanto)

must_not_include.note: Acqua is feminine singular; quanto agrees to quanta, not the plural quanti.
Even uncountable, acqua is feminine singular, so quanta not quanto.

explanation: How much water do you drink a day? = Quanta acqua bevi al giorno? Water cannot be counted, but quanto still agrees in gender and number with the noun. Acqua is feminine singular, so the form is quanta.

prompt: Completa: '____ costa questo cappuccino?'
explanation: How much does this cappuccino cost? = Quanto costa questo cappuccino? Here quanto means 'how much' as an adverb tied to the verb costare, and an adverb does not agree: it stays quanto whatever the price. The agreeing forms quanta/quanti/quante would need a noun to agree with, and there is none.
examiner_note: Instrument B per ITEM_SHAPE_no_change_forms: quanto is invariable here, so a blank cannot make invariability a real choice; the four inflections as options can.

prompt: Completa: 'Ho preparato dei biscotti. ____ ne vuoi?' (quanto)

markpoints.label: quanto as a pronoun, agreeing with the implied noun

must_not_include.note: Standing in for biscotti (masculine plural), quanto agrees to quanti even though the noun is not repeated.

explanation: I've made some biscuits. How many (of them) do you want? = Quanti ne vuoi? Even without repeating the noun, quanto agrees with what it stands for: the biscuits (biscotti) are masculine plural, so quanti. The little word ne means 'of them'.

prompt: Completa: '____ pane compriamo per la festa?'
explanation: How much bread shall we buy for the party? = Quanto pane compriamo per la festa? Quanto agrees with the noun it measures. Pane is masculine singular, so the masculine singular quanto is right. Quanta is feminine, quanti/quante are plural, none fitting one uncountable masculine noun.
examiner_note: Instrument B: the answer is quanto's base masculine singular, i.e. the citation form, so a free-text blank would let a copied cue win; MCQ makes the agreement a real choice.

prompt: Completa: '____ ti chiami?'
explanation: What is your name? = Come ti chiami? Italian asks a name with come (how), literally 'how do you call yourself?', not with che or cosa. The English 'what is your name' tempts che/cosa, but Italian fixes on come here.

prompt: Completa: '____ la stazione, per favore?' [where is]

any_phrases.note: Understood, but dove normally elides before è: dov'è.

explanation: Where is the station, please? = Dov'è la stazione, per favore? Before the verb è, dove drops its final -e and takes an apostrophe: dove è becomes dov'è. The full dove è is understood but sounds heavy; dov'è is the everyday form.
examiner_note: norm() folds the apostrophe, so dov'è and dov è mark alike; the elision is taught, not graded. Accent-off dov e falls to the estate-wide residue/accent miss flagged separately.

prompt: Completa: '____ finisce la scuola, a giugno o a luglio?'
explanation: When does school finish, in June or July? = Quando finisce la scuola, a giugno o a luglio? A choice between two times (June or July) is a time question, which Italian asks with quando (when). Dove asks place and perché asks reason, neither of which fits 'in June or July'.

prompt: Completa: '____ studi l'italiano, per lavoro o per piacere?'
explanation: Why do you study Italian, for work or for pleasure? = Perché studi l'italiano, per lavoro o per piacere? A reason (for work / for pleasure) is asked with perché (why). Come asks how and quando asks when, neither of which answers 'for what reason'.

prompt: Completa: '____ non hai risposto al messaggio?' [how come]

any_phrases.note: Also correct; come mai adds a note of surprise ('how come?').

explanation: How come you didn't reply to the message? = Come mai non hai risposto al messaggio? Come mai is a set phrase for 'how come / why', carrying a hint of surprise. Plain perché (why) works too; come mai adds the 'what on earth for?' colour.

prompt: Completa: '____ sei, italiano o straniero?' [where ... from]

must_not_include.note: Origin is di dove (from where); bare dove asks location, not where you come from.

explanation: Where are you from, Italian or foreign? = Di dove sei, italiano o straniero? Origin is asked with di dove (from where): the di supplies the 'from'. Bare dove would ask where you are right now, not where you come from.
examiner_note: Bare-dove guard nests in the correct 'di dove' but the positive wins first, so it only fires on the dropped-di attempt.

prompt: Completa: '____ aspetti l'autobus, da mezz'ora?' [since when]

must_not_include.note: Duration reaching the present is da quando (since when); bare quando asks a single moment.

explanation: Since when have you been waiting for the bus, for half an hour? = Da quando aspetti l'autobus, da mezz'ora? Duration reaching into the present (half an hour so far) is asked with da quando (since when): da adds the 'since'. Bare quando would ask at what moment, not from when.
examiner_note: Bare-quando guard nests in 'da quando' but the positive wins first.

prompt: Completa: '____ ha vinto la gara?'
explanation: Who won the race? = Chi ha vinto la gara? A race is won by a person, so the question word is chi (who). Che would ask 'what' and quale 'which of a set', neither of which fits a person acting.
examiner_note: Suppressed: the breadcrumb 'chi vs che vs quale' would tip that a choice is in play; the learner should read it from the sentence.

prompt: Completa: '____ vuoi da bere?'

markpoints.label: che cosa for an open thing

explanation: What do you want to drink? = Che cosa vuoi da bere? An open question about a thing (a drink, with no set listed) takes che cosa (also che or cosa). Chi is for people; quale needs a named set to pick from.

prompt: Completa: 'Ci sono due strade. ____ prendiamo, la prima o la seconda?'

markpoints.label: quale for selection from a set

explanation: There are two roads. Which do we take, the first or the second? = Quale prendiamo, la prima o la seconda? Choosing from a named set (two roads) is quale (which one). Che asks an open 'what', and chi is for people.

prompt: Completa: '____ costa un biglietto del cinema?'
explanation: How much does a cinema ticket cost? = Quanto costa un biglietto del cinema? A price is a quantity, asked with quanto (how much). Quale picks from a set and che asks 'what', neither of which asks an amount.

prompt: Completa: '____ è il tuo attore preferito?'
explanation: Who is your favourite actor? = Chi è il tuo attore preferito? An actor is a person, so it is chi (who), even though English 'who' can tempt che ('what'). Quale would ask 'which one' from a listed set.

prompt: Completa: '____ bello!'

markpoints.label: che for a bare adjective/noun exclamation

explanation: How lovely! = Che bello! Before a bare adjective or noun with no verb, the exclamation takes che: Che bello!, Che freddo!, Che sorpresa! Come needs a verb after it and quanto expresses quantity, so neither fits a plain 'how lovely'.

prompt: Completa: '____ sei gentile!'

markpoints.label: come before a verb in an exclamation

explanation: How kind you are! = Come sei gentile! When a verb follows (sei), the exclamation takes come: Come sei gentile!, Come piove! Che would stand before a bare adjective (Che gentile!) with no verb, and quanto expresses amount.

prompt: Completa: '____ storie! Non finisci mai di lamentarti.' (quanto)
explanation: What a lot of fuss! = Quante storie! In an exclamation of quantity, quanto agrees with its noun: storie is feminine plural, so quante. Literally 'how many stories', an idiom for making a fuss.

prompt: Completa: '____ pazienza hai con i bambini!' (quanto)
explanation: How much patience you have with the children! = Quanta pazienza hai con i bambini! Quanto agrees with the noun of quantity: pazienza is feminine singular, so quanta.

prompt: Completa: '____ hai speso per la macchina!'

markpoints.label: quanto (invariable) for quantity with a verb

explanation: How much you spent on the car! = Quanto hai speso per la macchina! Quantity with a verb (hai speso) is quanto, invariable here. Come would ask manner (how you spent it) and che sets up a noun/adjective exclamation, neither of which is 'how much'.
